panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Gross surgical specimen from a patient with ovarian mucinous cystadenoma; caption and article title directly support the diagnosis and show the gross multilocular cystic manifestation. B: H&E histopathology panel from the same ovarian mucinous cystadenoma case, showing the characteristic mucinous epithelial lining of cysts and glands. C: H&E histopathology panel demonstrating gastric foveolar-type mucinous epithelium, a recognized feature of ovarian mucinous cystadenoma, in the same patient. D: H&E histopathology panel from the same ovarian mucinous cystadenoma case, showing non-atypical basal nuclei and no invasion, consistent with a benign mucinous cystadenoma.

panels.figure_caption: Histopathological images of the ovarian cyst. (A) Grossly, a cut-open specimen of the ovary shows multiple cystic areas; (B) ovarian parenchyma shows multiple cysts and glands lined by simple, non-stratified mucinous epithelium (H&E; 2×); (C) the simple non-stratified mucinous epithelium resembles gastric foveolar type epithelium (H&E; 4×); (D) nuclei are small and basally located without cytological atypia. No invasion has been identified (H&E; 10×).

Left salpingo-oophorectomy was performed as the whole ovary was involved in the mass and the left tube was abnormally dilated and adherent to the mass (Figure 3). The size of the tumour was 42 × 28 × 25 cm with 7,250 kg in weight. Microscopic examination revealed a cyst lined by a single layer of non-ciliated columnar epithelium without stromal invasion, the picture of which is compatible with mucinous cystadenoma (Figure 4). Postoperative recovery was uneventful and the patient was discharged on the 5th postoperative day to be followed-up every 3 months.

The left ovary and uterus were unremarkable, and a right adnexectomy was performed. Intraoperative ascitic cytology was negative. On histological examination, the cyst wall was lined by simple non-stratified mucinous epithelium without atypia (Figure 2). The tissue specimen was made for every 1 cm of the cyst, and the atypical cell was not detected in any specimen. We diagnosed this case as a mucinous cystadenoma of the right ovary.

findings.label: Low-level echoes in loculated cyst fluid

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Ultrasound panel from a case report of a massive ovarian mucinous cystadenoma in a term pregnancy; caption states 'Ovarian cyst abutting the uterus with the placenta', showing a large smooth-walled ovarian cyst, a manifestation consistent with the article's confirmed mucinous cystadenoma. No demographic data given in caption/in-text. B: Caption explicitly describes a large multilocular cyst with homogeneous low-level internal echoes in the left adnexal region extending into the abdomen, the classic sonographic appearance of an ovarian mucinous cystadenoma in this case report. C: Same ultrasound study of the mucinous cystadenoma with caliper measurements (D1 26.56 cm, D2 19.75 cm, D3 13.35 cm) of the large loculated cyst containing low-level echoes, matching the captioned dimensions of the cysts.
panels.attribution_text: Sinha et al. Massive Ovarian Mucinous Cystadenoma Complicating Term Birth.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.64054. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Ultrasonographic image of the ovarian cyst. (A) Ovarian cyst abutting the uterus with the placenta; (B) large multilocular cyst with homogenous low-level echoes in the left adnexal region extending into the abdomen; (C) dimensions of the cysts: 26.56 cm × 19.75 cm × 13.35 cm.
in_text_mentions: Sections from the appendix showed features of chronic appendicitis with no features of dysplasia or malignancy. On follow-up after six weeks, the patient was in good health with no complaints. Figure 1 shows an ultrasonographic image of a large multilocular cyst with low-level internal echoes in the left adnexal region extending in the abdomen of dimensions 26 cm × 19 cm × 13 cm, abutting the uterus with the placenta. plate_findings.evidence: Transabdominal ultrasonography showing a transverse view of the left upper quadrant ... of a cystic lesion; in-text: 'A transabdominal ultrasound scan (USS) showed a cyst with no solid components'

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real patient transabdominal ultrasound (disease-focused article title on ovarian mucinous cystadenoma) showing a large cystic lesion extending to the left upper quadrant, consistent with the captioned cystic manifestation of the ovarian mucinous cystadenoma; no solid components described. Measurement calipers and body markers are annotated. B: Real patient transabdominal ultrasound of the lower abdomen showing the large thin-walled cystic ovarian lesion in a case of ovarian mucinous cystadenoma (disease-focused article title); in-text mentions a cyst without solid components and minimal free intraperitoneal fluid. Measurement calipers and body markers are annotated.
panels.attribution_text: Somagutta et al. A Rare Case of Massive Ovarian Mucinous Cystadenoma With Postmenopausal Bleeding.. Cureus 2020. doi:10.7759/cureus.10198. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Transabdominal ultrasonography showing a transverse view of the left upper quadrant (A) and lower abdomen (B) of a cystic lesion.
in_text_mentions: the results were normal. The patient did not take any regular medications, including hormonal therapy. She had no family history of the bowel, breast, ovarian, and uterine cancer. Physical examination revealed abdominal distension with a large mass of 35 cm above the pubic symphysis. There was no fluid wave thrill, no focal tenderness, rebound, or guarding of the abdomen upon examination. Normal cervix with vaginal atrophy was noted. Her blood work was unremarkable. A transabdominal ultrasound scan (USS) showed a cyst with no solid components with minimal free intraperitoneal fluid (Figure 1).
